m: उशनस् m. आ (Pāṇ. vii, 1, 94; Ved. acc. आम्; Ved. loc. and dat. ए; voc. अस्, अ, and अन्, Kāś. on Pāṇ.) N. of an ancient sage with the patronymic Kāvya, RV.; AV. iv, 29, 6; Kauś. (in later times identified with Śukra, the teacher of the Asuras, who presides over the planet Venus)
N. of the planet Venus, MBh.; Yājñ.; Pañcat. &c.
N. of the author of a Dharma-śāstra, Hcat. i, 5
(उशनसः स्तोम m. N. of a verse (RV. v, 29, 9) to be muttered by one who thinks himself poisoned, ĀśvŚr. v, 9, 1.)
a: उशनस् — m. [वश्-कनसि संप्र˚ Uṇ. 4. 238] (Nom. sing. उशना; Voc. sing. उशनन्, उशन, उशनः) N. of Śukra, regent of the planet Venus, son of Bhṛgu and preceptor of the Asuras. In the Vedas he has the epithet Kāvya given to him, probably because he was noted for his wisdom; cf. Bg. 10. 37; कवीनामुशना कविः. He is also known as a writer on civil and religious law (Y. 1. 4), and as an authority on civil polity; शास्त्रमुशनसा प्रणीतं Pt. 5; अध्यापितस्योशनसापि नीतिं Ku. 3. 6.
